defect: real_server eprintln! diagnostics can panic when a host-owned collector stderr pipe loses its reader. Terminal owner/budget/server records precede the authenticated cleanup ACK; the stderr-drain worker also emits metadata before returning its actual result. Panic can therefore skip ACK or change a successful drain into JoinError.
historical_attribution: The e340 failed sample retained verified owner/budget records but no terminal signal/errno; neither EPIPE nor SIGTERM is claimed as that exact sample cause.
correction: Only diagnostic stderr write errors are ignored, using a local non-panicking writer with unchanged formatting. Actual transport, stderr-drain quota/read result, owner/budget/process cleanup and authenticated ACK still determine success or failure.

regression.mechanism: Real Unix child test process waits on stdin until its parent has closed the diagnostic stderr reader. It then calls the actual drain_stderr on real child stderr: normal EOF must succeed and >1MiB must still refuse. The parent requires normal successful exit and an exact completion marker.
regression.timeout_behavior: kill and reap the exact test child, then fail
regression.before: fails on eprintln implementation: closed stderr aborted cleanup
regression.limits: Local subprocess/diagnostic-drain proof, not a native namespace-owner or daemon ACK acceptance claim.
